scenario_provenance.archetype_label: Multi-focus on Practices 1 & 2 (formulate questions; collect/represent data)
validity_rules: Unit 1 random-sampling methods only: SRS, stratified, cluster, systematic
non-random convenience and voluntary-response plans must be identified as non-random
stratified samples units within every stratum; cluster samples all units in selected clusters

sources.note: the item stem's verb must match the scored demand

prompt: A researcher wants to study which library services they used last month among adult patrons of a county library system. Sampling plan: The researcher records responses from patrons at the front desk of the main branch on Saturday morning. Which choice best describes the sampling method?

options.text: Stratified random sample, because the researcher should randomly choose whole branch library groups and include everyone in them.

misconception_source.label: Thought stratified sampling means sampling whole groups

sources.note: stratified sampling takes a random sample within every stratum; sampling all observational units in selected clusters is cluster sampling

options.text: Cluster sample, because the population is divided into groups such as branch library before the sample is chosen.

misconception_source.label: Confused stratified sampling with cluster sampling

sources.note: CED vocabulary distinguishes SRS, stratified, cluster, and systematic sampling; cluster samples all units within selected clusters, while stratified samples within every stratum

options.text: Not a random sample; it is a convenience sample because the units are easy to reach.
SRS, because any member of the population could have ended up in the response group.

misconception_source.label: Called a convenience or voluntary-response sample random

sources.note: 2025 CR Report Q2 flags sampling-method/bias vocabulary errors and incomplete random-sampling procedures; convenience and voluntary response are non-random biased methods
